items.title: An exponential upper bound on the number of large sets with a small edge boundary in a product graph
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the counting lemma for large sets with a small edge boundary (author lemma at source lines 714-716, label lem:small-boundary-sets): for a in the stated range, at most exp(2a/log d) sets of size a have an edge boundary below a log^2 d. The proof (source lines 718-743) has genuine content: it restricts to a sub-product on a set I of m = log_2(log^5 d) coordinates, applies the author's isoperimetric inequality on that sub-product to force any set with a small boundary to interact non-trivially with few of the fibres, converts that into a binomial-product bound on the number of admissible sets, and then optimises over m and over the choice of I to reach the exponential bound (proof lines 719-742). The lemma is one of the two counting inputs to the size bound on obstructions. H2.
